eligibility.evidence: Studies 1 and 2 compare GPT-4’s emotional appraisal and attribution with human ratings using established emotion-eliciting stimuli and a human-annotated corpus (Studies 1–2).

A.title: GPT-4 Cognition Emulates Average-Human from a Third-Person Perspective
A.venue: 11th International Conference on Affective Computing and Intelligent Interaction (ACII)

paradigms.name: Appraisal and emotion ratings of crafted emotion-evoking stimuli (third-person appraisal derivation, emotion attribution, and appraisal-to-emotion mapping)
paradigms.source_paper: Skerry and Saxe (2015), “Neural representations of emotion are organized around abstract event features”

paradigms.name: Emotion and appraisal attribution for self-reported vignettes, compared with authors and external readers

D.population: Study 1 participants rating crafted stimuli; Study 2 authors and five human readers, with crowd-enVENT annotations
D.metric: Correlation with human mean ratings; classification accuracy; Krippendorff’s alpha agreement

E.headline: GPT-4’s ratings and emotion attributions align closely with average readers, and in Study 1 it classifies intended emotions more accurately than human participants.

G.notes: A referee would ask how GPT-4 accuracy was statistically compared with human accuracy, given repeated prompts on each stimulus and differing human/model response variability. Study 2’s reported agreement comparisons and statistical tests are not detailed in the extracted text.
